entries.topic: Who can become a citizen: Law of Return and Nationality Law vs US birthright and naturalisation; aliyah and naturalisation series; family-unification ban; East Jerusalem; revocation

claims.text: Nationality Law 1952 s.4: a person born in Israel acquires nationality at birth if 'his father or mother was an Israel national'; born abroad, if a parent held Israeli nationality. s.5: naturalisation of an adult requires presence, residence in the preceding five years, a right to permanent residence, intention to settle, some Hebrew and renunciation of prior nationality, at the Interior Minister's discretion, with a loyalty declaration. s.11(b) (original text): the Minister may terminate nationality for 'an act constituting a breach of allegiance'.
Aliyah and Integration Ministry report (June 2026): 22,522 immigrants in 2025, about 10,000 fewer than 2024; Western countries' share rose from 21% to 38%; 3,781 from the United States.
2022: about 70,000 immigrants from 95 countries, the highest in 23 years; Russia 37,364 and Ukraine 14,680 (1 Jan–1 Dec 2022, Jewish Agency and Ministry).

US naturalisations: 878,460 in FY2023, down 9.4% from 969,380 in FY2022; FY2021 813,860; FY2020 628,250; FY2019 843,590; annual averages ~210,000 in the 1980s, 500,000 in the 1990s, 680,000 in the 2000s, 730,100 in 2010–19; median 7 years as LPR; Mexico top country of birth (111,460).
US naturalisation requires age 18+, five years' lawful permanent residence (three if married to a US citizen), basic English, civics knowledge and good moral character.
Pew: 51.9m immigrants in the US in June 2025 (15.4%), down from a record 53.3m in January 2025; unauthorised immigrant population a record 14m in 2023; 46% of immigrants naturalised citizens in 2023.

Trump v. Barbara, No. 25-365, decided 30 June 2026, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts: children born in the US to parents unlawfully or temporarily present are citizens at birth under the Fourteenth Amendment; EO 14160 remains enjoined. Dissents by Thomas (joined by Gorsuch) and Alito (joined by Gorsuch) argued the clause requires domicile.

Supreme Court (Israel) on 4 December 2022 asked the state whether it would amend the 2022 Citizenship and Entry law; Knesset extended it for one year on 5 March 2023 without amendments; nine petitions pending; humanitarian permits capped at 2018 level (58).
Adalah (2019): the law, renewed annually since 2003, bars Palestinian citizens married to West Bank or Gaza residents from living with spouses in Israel; upheld 2006 and 2012, the 2012 ruling 6–5.

Reuters 2015: ~300,000 East Jerusalem Palestinians; citizenship applications 114 in 2003, 800–1,000 a year recently (JIIS); 2012–13: 1,434 applications, 189 approved, 169 rejected; about 24,000 since 1967 (~10%) per Khalil Tafakji.

Al Jazeera: February 2023 law eases revocation of citizenship or residency of Palestinians convicted of terrorism who receive PA payments; in February 2026 Netanyahu signed the first orders revoking two men's citizenship and ordering deportation, subject to district court review within 30 days; only 5% of East Jerusalem Palestinians had obtained citizenship since 1967 (Haaretz 2022).

entries.topic: Asylum and enforcement: Israel's African asylum seekers (Anti-Infiltration Law, Holot, 2018 plan) vs US refugees, asylum, removals, ICE funding

claims.text: HRW: 64,000 asylum seekers and migrants entered via Sinai 2006–2013, including 50,000 Sudanese and Eritreans; Israel denied 100% of Sudanese and over 99% of Eritrean asylum claims; Sept 2013 High Court struck down the January 2012 amendment to the 1954 Prevention of Infiltration Law; Knesset passed a new amendment Dec 2013; on 22 Sept 2014 the court voided the Holot provisions (7–2) and one-year detention of new arrivals (6–3), giving 90 days; about 7,000 Eritreans and Sudanese 'coerced into leaving'; after the Egypt fence irregular entries 'fallen to near zero'.

+972: Holot opened late 2013 and closed 14 March 2018; more than 13,000 held there over its life; peak near 60,000 asylum seekers in 2012, about 38,000 in March 2018; 3,959 left under 'voluntary return' 2013–2017; January 2018 plan gave three months to leave or face indefinite imprisonment or deportation to Rwanda or Uganda; High Court interim injunction 15 March 2018.

MRG (Dec 2025): an estimated 25,000 African asylum seekers, mostly Eritrean and Sudanese; recognition below 1%; the 2 April 2018 UNHCR agreement (resettle about half in Western states, status for the rest) was cancelled the next day under coalition pressure; about 1,700 transferred to Uganda 2015–2018; High Court later ruled indefinite detention unlawful without formal reception agreements.

CRS: EO 14163 (20 Jan 2025) suspended refugee entry; FY2025 ceiling 125,000, admissions 38,102; FY2026 ceiling 7,500 'primarily' for Afrikaners, raised in May 2026 to 17,500, still the lowest in program history; 7,730 admitted through 30 June 2026, nearly all South African; FY1980 ceiling 231,700 and admissions 207,116; lowest admissions 11,411 in FY2021; ceilings at or above 67,000 every year before FY2018.
Pew (2014): a record 438,421 deportations in FY2013 per then-current DHS data; 83% without a judge; more than 2 million since Obama took office.
USAFacts: ICE deportations about 320,000 in FY2025, up 18% from FY2024; detention book-ins 365,500 (+29.7%); CBP enforcement actions 3.3m (2023), 2.3m (2024), 391,000 (2025).

Brennan Center: the July 2025 budget act gave about $170bn for immigration enforcement over four years, $75bn to ICE including about $45bn for detention, about $65bn to CBP of which nearly $47bn for the border wall; ICE's ~$28.7bn for FY2025 nearly triple FY2024.
MPI (Nov 2025): immigration court backlog about 3.8 million cases by mid-2025, more than doubled FY2021–24; more than 139 immigration judges fired; about 68% in removal proceedings without a lawyer.

RAICES: on 24 April 2026 the D.C. Circuit (RAICES v. Noem, No. 25-5243) held the executive cannot use its 212(f) suspension-of-entry power to 'override asylum laws established by Congress' or create expulsion procedures without authorisation; likely to be appealed.

claims.text: Trump v. Barbara (30 June 2026): Roberts for the Court, joined by Sotomayor, Kagan, Barrett and Jackson; Jackson concurring; Kavanaugh concurring in the judgment in part and dissenting in part; Thomas dissenting, joined by Gorsuch; Alito dissenting; Gorsuch dissenting separately.

HRW 2014: the Israeli government called Sudanese and Eritreans 'work infiltrators' and argued not deporting them gave adequate protection; described Holot as an 'open residency center'; Interior Minister Gideon Sa'ar said he could not accept the verdict, warning borders would be overrun by illegal infiltrators.

CRS: EO 14163 stated that entry of refugees under USRAP 'would be detrimental to the interests of the United States'; more than 98% of FY2025 admissions arrived in the first four months; FY2026 ceiling of 17,500 'the lowest in the history of the USRAP'.
